review.incorrectAreAlgorithmic: Every incorrect source read in full; each prints a numerically wrong answer on valid tests (format/debug-only failures not counted).
review.independentOracle: Per-app unread counters, a monotone global prefix pointer, and per-app 'read up to index' marks from type-2 events; O(q). Cross-checked against literal full-list simulation on 20000 random small event sequences.
review.officialTests: Basis 'generated': official_tests_complete=false (4 of 99 official rows, all present as 0001-0004 and token-equal), plus all 25 open-r1 generated tests for 704/A from the sha-verified pinned generated_tests/test_cases_0704.parquet (all present, token-equal, oracle-equal), plus 152 worker-generated pairs.

I re-ran qualification/generator.py (seed 0) in the pinned sandbox: its output hash equals both repeatOutputHashes and reproduces exactly the 152 authored package pairs (pairsHash matches). My own oracle independently agrees with every expected output.
review.oracleResult: All 181 package tests and all samples pass a strict format/range parse; every expected output equals my oracle; all upstream official rows equal my oracle.
review.sandbox: Own harness (sha256 c582ff42...983d0d; 704A re-judged with a token-hash variant because outputs exceed 200 bytes; not worker pool_harness): pinned python@sha256:5887f265...05d3, --network=none, --read-only, --user=65534, --cap-drop=ALL, no-new-privileges, pids<=32, 1 CPU, 2560m memory, RLIMIT_CPU/AS at problem limits, bounded output, launched from env -i shell without credentials; g++ -O2 -std=c++17 -DONLINE_JUDGE.
review.singleAnswer: Output is uniquely determined by the input; token comparison is correct; no special checker or float tolerance.
review.statement: Statement bounds explicit (1 ≤ n, q ≤ 300 000; 1 ≤ type ≤ 3, 1 ≤ x ≤ n, 1 ≤ t ≤ q; at least t type-1 events precede a type-3 event); no exponent flattening, no normalization.
review.submissionProvenance: All sources byte-identical (sha256) to rows in pinned open-r1/codeforces-submissions shards (shard sha256 verified independently); upstream verdict/problem/language match; for every incorrect source the first failing package test equals upstream passedTestCount+1.
